title: The Cry Hidden in a Cat's Purr
central_question: Why does a hungry cat's purr sound so urgent?
central_fact: In a 2009 study, solicitation purrs contained a pronounced high-frequency component around 380 Hz, and listeners rated them more urgent and less pleasant than ordinary purrs.
takeaway: The cry is a real acoustic feature, but it does not prove that a cat is calculating or suffering.

hook.text: That hungry purr has a cry hidden inside.

scenes.narration: That hungry purr has a cry hidden inside.

visual.description: A gray cat sits on a kitchen floor beside a ceramic food bowl, looking up toward an off-screen person. Its mouth is closed and its throat is relaxed, as if a low purr is running. Soft morning light and a quiet, uncluttered kitchen.
visual.subject: one gray cat with a white chest and pale yellow eyes
visual.motion: slow push-in; the cat blinks once and holds a calm gaze
visual.framing: vertical 9:16, cat's face in the upper middle third, bowl at the bottom edge
visual.continuity: same gray cat, kitchen, and ceramic bowl in every scene

scenes.narration: A purr is not one flat sound. It can carry a low rumble and, sometimes, a higher, cry-like layer.

visual.description: A warm abstract visualization of a purr: a broad, slow undulating ribbon of amber light fills the lower half of the frame, while a thinner, brighter thread rises through it. The shapes are smooth and non-literal, with no labels or readable marks.
visual.subject: two layered ribbons of light, one low and broad, one higher and thinner
visual.motion: slow lateral drift; the bright thread gradually becomes more distinct
visual.framing: vertical 9:16, ribbons centered with generous negative space above
visual.continuity: same amber palette and fine grain as the kitchen scenes; no sudden style shift

scenes.narration: In 2009, researchers recorded purrs from ten cats in two situations: ordinary purring and purring while soliciting food.

visual.description: The same gray cat stands beside the ceramic bowl in the kitchen. An owner's hand lowers a small portion of plain food into the bowl and withdraws. The cat watches the hand, then looks toward the bowl without rushing or vocalizing visibly.
visual.subject: the same gray cat and an owner's hand, no visible face
visual.motion: gentle tilt down from hand to bowl
visual.framing: vertical 9:16, cat and bowl in the lower middle third, clean space above
visual.continuity: same kitchen, bowl, and cat; the owner wears a plain gray sleeve

scenes.narration: The solicitation purrs held a pronounced high-frequency peak, averaging about 380 hertz, within a broader purr.

visual.description: A closer abstract view of the same layered sound image. The bright thread now has a clear, narrow crest near the upper third of the frame, while the broad amber ribbon continues below. Tiny particles of light drift along both paths, and no labels appear.
visual.subject: the bright upper thread and the broad lower ribbon of light
visual.motion: slow push-in toward the crest, then a gentle hold
visual.framing: vertical 9:16, crest on the upper-third line, lower ribbon across the bottom third
visual.continuity: same amber palette, grain, and ribbon shapes as the previous abstract scene

scenes.narration: Fifty listeners heard both recordings at equal volume. They rated the solicitation purrs as more urgent and less pleasant, even when they did not own cats.

visual.description: The same gray cat sits beside the bowl while an owner's hand rests on the counter nearby. The cat looks toward the hand, half-closes its eyes, and stays calm. A soft reflection of the kitchen window moves across the ceramic bowl.
visual.subject: the same gray cat, the ceramic bowl, and an owner's resting hand
visual.motion: very slow lateral slide from the cat's face to the bowl
visual.framing: vertical 9:16, cat in the middle third, hand and bowl in the lower third
visual.continuity: same cat, bowl, counter, and gray sleeve; no other animals

scenes.narration: So the cry in the purr is real, not a clever plan. It is one more way a cat can get a human to listen.

visual.description: The same gray cat rests on a windowsill beside the bowl, which holds a little plain food. The cat's eyes are half closed and its breathing is slow. The camera pulls back gently to show the quiet kitchen, then fades.
visual.subject: the same gray cat resting beside the ceramic bowl
visual.motion: slow pull-back; the cat remains still and calm
visual.framing: vertical 9:16, cat in the lower middle third, window light above
visual.continuity: same windowsill, bowl, and gray cat; no new people or animals

claims.text: Solicitation purrs contain a high-frequency voiced component with a peak in the 220-520 Hz range, averaging about 380 Hz, embedded in the low-frequency purr.
claims.limits: The range and mean describe the recorded purrs in this study, not every purr from every cat.

claims.text: The study recorded purrs from ten cats in solicitation and non-solicitation situations and played them to fifty human listeners at equal amplitude.
claims.limits: Ten cats and fifty listeners are modest samples; the recordings were edited into short sequences for playback.

claims.text: Listeners rated solicitation purrs as more urgent and less pleasant than non-solicitation purrs.
claims.limits: The ratings measure human perception of the sounds, not the cat's intent or emotional state.

claims.text: The authors interpret the embedded high-frequency component as a cry-like signal that can make a solicitation purr harder to ignore.
claims.evidence_level: authors' interpretation of acoustic and playback data
claims.limits: The study shows an acoustic feature and a listener response; it does not directly demonstrate deliberate manipulation by cats.

claims.text: The result does not show that cats consciously calculate the effect or that the purr indicates distress.
claims.limits: The experiment was not designed to test intention, learning, or welfare state.

visual_policy.style: Observational real-footage montage built from third-party pet clips, natural light, calm pacing, and species-correct behavior.
visual_policy.anatomy: Every animal must be species-correct and anatomically coherent. Multiple individuals may appear across clips; reject malformed, uncanny, or merged animals.
visual_policy.welfare: The cat is calm, fed a small plain portion, and never shown starving, begging in distress, or eating unsafe food. No restraint or forced interaction. Reject any clip with staged distress, restraint, injury, aggression, or a visible watermark.
visual_policy.continuity: Keep the question, tone, and caption position consistent across clips. Do not imply that different animals are the same individual. Avoid repeated or watermarked clips.
visual_policy.disclosure: Real-footage montage using third-party clips for illustration; not documentary footage or scientific evidence.

youtube.title: The Cry Hidden in a Cat's Purr

notes: Say the purr contains a cry-like component; do not claim cats cry on purpose or that the sound is a human infant cry.
The study measured listener ratings, not feline intent. Keep the narration on the evidence.

risk_notes: Do not use the word 'manipulation' as an established fact; the study describes an acoustic signal and a human response.
Avoid implying that a cat who produces this purr is neglected or hungry; the recordings were made in ordinary feeding interactions.
